transcript: The other night, Paul and I saw Brooklyn Laundry, a new play by John Patrick Stanley at MTC. Cecily Strong and David Zayas star as Fran and Owen in this somewhat rom-com, romanticized-the-mundane kind of play, and I thought their performances and chemistry carried the show. They both play rather ordinary people struggling with relatively ordinary problems —loneliness, reality, and maybe even self-sabotage. In the opening scene, which in my opinion is the strongest and most interesting one, they meet for the first time at Owen's laundromat, and they're intrigued by one another, and they plan to go out to dinner. In the rest of the play, we see more of Fran’s life and how the forces of her reality fuel a sense of longing and insignificance that she's constantly trying to overcome. The ideas were charming, although I thought the plot felt contrived and it didn't really go anywhere for me. On the other hand, one could argue that the plot is universal and that its flatness supports this. Paul loved it, so I think it all depends on how you look at it. With that, another playbill for my collection.
